project.name: BLACKHEART Security Framework
project.author: Roshan
project.note: No company, legal entity, attorney, certification or registration is claimed. These documents have not been reviewed by a lawyer. Where enforceability depends on jurisdiction or legal advice, the document says so rather than asserting it.

requirements.active_operation_definition: Any operation that sends a request over a network: every command that takes --scope, and any direct call into workbench.http_client.request().

acceptance.note: The state directory may be moved by environment variable; the acceptance itself cannot be satisfied by one. An empty or missing directory blocks active operations exactly as an unaccepted policy does.

enforcement.reason: Every socket in the framework is opened there, so the check sits under the network boundary rather than beside it.
enforcement.documented_residual: The acceptance acknowledgement can be forged by a person with local write access to the state directory, because it records an acknowledgement rather than a secret. The scope check that follows cannot be forged this way: it reads the authorization file the operator supplied.

acquisition_rules.resources_requiring_authorized_access: require the operator's own authorized credentials
acquisition_rules.paywalled_or_subscription_resources: do not circumvent; record blocked and name the authorized route
acquisition_rules.signed_urls: do not extend, guess or reuse; record expired
acquisition_rules.licensed_content: record the licence note; do not strip notices; do not redistribute
acquisition_rules.blocked_representation: A blocked resource is recorded as blocked with its HTTP status and the route that is authorized. It is never represented as a failed challenge to be overcome.
acquisition_rules.execution: Never execute, import, install or run anything acquired. No macros. No binaries.

prohibited_actions: Unauthorized access to any system, or testing any target without the authorization required for it
Bypassing authentication, authorization, MFA, CAPTCHA or any other access control
Bypassing, evading or defeating a WAF, IDS, rate limit or security control
Circumventing a paywall, subscription check, DRM, licensing control or signed-URL expiry
Accessing private storage, private repositories or another person's data without authorization
Obtaining, using or transferring credentials, tokens, session cookies or keys that are not the operator's own authorized access material
Collecting personal data beyond what the authorized engagement requires
Destructive, disruptive or denial-of-service testing without explicit authorization
Deploying malware, ransomware, persistence or any unauthorized payload
Exploiting a target without authorization, or automatically exploiting anything the workbench observes
Fabricating evidence, findings, downloads, scans, statistics or successful exploitation
Promoting a potential or unverified observation into a confirmed finding
Representing the framework's output, or possession of the framework, as authorization
Using the framework to surveil, defraud, harass or abuse any person or infrastructure
Executing, importing or installing anything acquired by the framework
allowed_actions: Testing infrastructure you own or operate
Testing a target for which you hold written authorization from someone entitled to grant it
Testing local test environments and the loopback fixtures shipped with this repository
Authorized security research within an agreed scope, budget and window
Authorized acquisition of public resources, and of resources you are authorized to access
Authorized incident evidence collection, read-only, within scope
Reading, hashing and reporting on evidence you already hold
